title: How should the Brass Aneroid be built?
question: Decide what the build answers to: an approved comp, or a written contract.

options.label: Comp-led
options.thesis: The comp you just chose, plus two variations, goes in front of you; the approved one becomes law and the finished widget is audited against it side by side.
options.viewport: Two more comps varying the dial layout (sub-dial placement, counter position, bezel density), then you approve one before any Swift is written.
options.risk: Boldest result, but expect fix rounds to match the comp's brass and glass, and one more approval stop before code.

options.label: Code-led
options.thesis: No further comps. The ambition moves into a written contract (first viewport, signature detail, night mode) and the finished widget is audited against that in behaviour.
materials: chosen comp as critique reference only
options.viewport: Straight to building in SwiftUI. The comp you picked returns at the end as the reference for what the build dared or missed.
options.risk: Faster to a working widget, but materials drawn in code drift toward flat unless the contract is held hard.
